summary.headline: Bigbloc Q2 FY27 revenue rose ~23% YoY to INR 83 crore and EBITDA ~74% to INR 3 crore, with October the record sales month.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR 83 crore, up around 23% YoY, driven mainly by volume; sales volume grew 13% to 2,25,241 cubic metres. EBITDA rose 74% YoY to about INR 3 crore, with margin up 116 bps to 3.98%, while the net loss widened to about INR 2.75 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was about INR 162 crore (+31%), EBITDA about INR 10 crore (margin 5.93%, +334 bps) and net loss about INR 3.5 crore. Management said input costs rose 8-10% and only 5-7% has been passed on so far, with the balance targeted for the next quarter.

segments.name: AAC blocks
segments.commentary: About 87-88% of H1 FY27 volume; manufactured at all 4 plants. Management said red bricks are about 10-15% costlier than AAC blocks, with conversion ongoing.

segments.name: AAC panels
segments.commentary: About 5-6% of H1 FY27 turnover; made at one plant. New orders include AdaniConneX data centre in Hyderabad, bullet train stations, ITC, Foxconn and Embassy Group work.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: About 5-6% of H1 FY27 turnover; in-house manufacturing started in Q1 FY27 after white-labelling. Plant utilisation is low; management sees potential revenue of about INR 20-25 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects utilisation to reach up to 75% in H2 FY27, from 68-69% in H1.
Input cost pass-through: the 5-7% differential is to be passed on in the upcoming quarter; further increases to be passed on as H2 demand is seasonally stronger.
Operational efficiency measures (electric forklifts, boiler automation) expected to improve EBITDA margin by about 2-3%, completed in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Further capacity expansion to be decided in the next 1-2 quarters, as utilisation is at 95%+ in some plants.
Gradual price revisions planned across markets while staying competitive.
capex_capacity: Utilisation was 68.74% in H1 FY27 versus about 56-57% in H1 FY26; management said October 2026 was the highest monthly turnover and volume ever.

A 57,000 sq m land parcel in Madhya Pradesh has approvals in place (including CPCB plan pass), but construction has not started due to the economic and geopolitical outlook; expansion decision in 1-2 quarters.
Transition from rented forklifts to an owned electric fleet, to be completed across all 4 plants in Q3 FY27.
Boiler automation under way at 3 plants, expected to be completed by the next quarter.
Management is not aware of major new AAC capacity in its operating regions; some new industrial units have reportedly shut or are up for sale.
demand_pricing: Input costs rose 8-10% (production cost up 8-12% per CBM, per management); 5-7% has been passed on so far, with the rest targeted in the next quarter.
Lime prices rose 3-4% in Q2 versus Q1; aluminium powder rose 15-20% in Q2, partly reversing in October; cement broadly flat; pond ash cost up 2-3% on diesel-driven transport.
Coal and transport costs rose and drove the increase in other operating expenses in Q2.
Industry average realisation is about INR 3,500-3,600 per cubic metre; management says realisations fell in FY26 and are now being improved.
Logistics is about 20-30% of total volume cost. Management says there is little pricing pressure, and volumes keep growing.
Customer retention is about 60-65% over the last few years; product can be sold up to 300-350 km from plants.
Receivable recovery cycle is 70-80 days; credit insurance taken from Tata AIG for large corporate customers.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling inflation and how much can it pass on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs rose 8-10% and 5-7% was passed on; the rest is expected to be passed on as H2 demand improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the price gap between red bricks and AAC blocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Red bricks are about 10-15% more expensive than AAC blocks, varying by region because of freight, since red brick density is about 3x that of AAC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply-demand picture and the funding plan for expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No major new capacity in the operating regions and no pricing pressure; expansion will be considered in 1-2 quarters. Debt-to-equity is about 1.4x, or about 1.2x with promoter unsecured loans treated as equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating expenses rise sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly transportation and energy costs, as coal prices rose sharply.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin under pressure and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, plus monsoon-related under-recovery. Management expects the pass-through and 75% utilisation in H2 to help.

qa_highlights.question: Will AAC panels rise as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Panels are made at one plant and are a new category; recent wins include ITC and bullet train stations, with more large orders said to be close.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (coal, lime, aluminium powder, diesel-linked freight) is only partly passed on; 5-7% of the 8-12% increase is still to be recovered.
Q2 net loss of ~INR 2.75 crore and H1 loss of ~INR 3.5 crore despite EBITDA growth, so finance and depreciation costs need watching.
Receivables of about INR 70 crore with a 70-80 day collection cycle, amid a liquidity squeeze in the market.
Capacity utilisation target of 75% in H2 FY27 versus 69% in H1; the October record needs to hold through Q3.
Construction chemicals plant utilisation is low; the INR 20-25 crore revenue potential is management's estimate only.
Timing of Madhya Pradesh expansion and the funding plan are undecided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and volumes, citing the record October and a strong H2 outlook. More cautious on margins, which management attributes to input inflation, monsoon effects and a calibrated pricing approach. Evasive on the timing of the Madhya Pradesh capacity and the funding details.
key_quotes: This reached an important milestone in October 2026 when Bigbloc recorded its highest ever monthly turnover and sales volume.
We have taken a calibrated approach to pricing rather than passing through the full increase in input costs immediately.
We are quite confident of achieving a better utilization up to 75% in H2.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 57,000 sq m Madhya Pradesh parcel has approvals but construction has not started, and management defers the decision by 1-2 quarters, so no new capacity is confirmed live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation is 69.34% in Q2 and 68.74% in H1 versus about 56-57% a year ago, with management targeting up to 75% in H2 FY27 and a record October.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says further capacity expansion will be decided in 1-2 quarters because some plants run at 95%+, but utilisation is only 69% on average and the Madhya Pradesh build is deferred.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident of up to 75% utilisation in H2 from 68.74% in H1, and October was the record month, but has not formally raised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input costs rose 8-12% per CBM with only 5-7% passed on, and Q2 net loss was about INR 2.75 crore, so margin and profit targets depend on pass-through holding.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Construction chemicals in-house manufacturing started in Q1 FY27 with management seeing INR 20-25 crore potential, but no firm launch date was given and panel wins are not new products.

rows.label: Pass-through of remaining input cost increase
rows.why: Only 5-7% of the 8-10% input cost rise has been passed on, and management targets the balance in the next quarter while industry realisation is about INR 3,500-3,600 per cubic metre.

rows.label: AAC panel orders from data centres and transit
rows.why: Panels are about 5-6% of H1 turnover, and new orders include AdaniConneX Hyderabad, bullet train stations, ITC and Foxconn, with management saying more large orders are close.

rows.label: Owned electric forklift fleet and boiler automation
rows.why: Forklift transition across all 4 plants is set for Q3 FY27 and boiler automation at 3 plants is due by the next quarter, which together support the 2-3% margin uplift.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, the record October and the 75% H2 utilisation target, but cautious on margins and evasive on the timing and funding of the Madhya Pradesh expansion; analysts focused on input cost pass-through, the margin path and the net loss.
